entries.subject: Disc-resolved images or interferometric imaging of WASP-76
entries.finding: The disc is about 0.09 mas across at 189 pc; no image or interferometric diameter exists. The sphere carries its Gaia color and a model limb.
entries.revisitWhen: A reconstructed image of the star's surface is published.

entries.subject: WASP-76 B, the bound K-type companion 0.44 arcsec away
entries.finding: Its separation, contrast and temperature are published (Ehrenreich et al. 2020, Methods; Southworth et al. 2020) but not an orbit, so it is not placed. Its light is inside the Gaia BP/RP spectrum that colors WASP-76.
entries.revisitWhen: An orbit or a separate object package for the companion is wanted.

entries.subject: The spin axis of WASP-76
entries.finding: Ehrenreich et al. (2020) measure only the sky-projected angle to the orbit, 61.28 degrees; the axis's tilt to the line of sight is not measured, so the display axis is celestial north.
entries.revisitWhen: A paper measures the stellar inclination.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 6,329 K and log g 4.11 (u1 0.368, u2 0.308): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. Gravity: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-76.json: 4.113.
